Data:Next.numa.json.label: Numa Next
Data:Next.numa.json.desc: The next season will be Numa.

Data:Night.killes.json.label: Unsociable Hours
Data:Night.killes.json.startdescription: The house is dark; the Killes will be tucked up in bed. I should be, too.

Data:Night.rectory.json.label: Unsociable Hours
Data:Night.rectory.json.startdescription: The rectory is dark, and Terrence the housekeeper is probably aprowl. I should return after dawn.

Data:Night.smithy.json.label: Unsociable Hours
Data:Night.smithy.json.startdescription: The smithy is dark, and Denzil values his sleep. I should return after dawn.

Data:Nillycant.json.Label: Nillycant
Data:Nillycant.json.Desc: The encaustum terminale of the Third History. It's the bleak white-blue of Winter. It has spawned an itinerant order of secret celebrants who regard Worms as semi-gods, and who are sometimes called on to celebrate difficult funerals. [Use an Encaustum ink with your Journal to make Determinations and record Histories. If the Hours listen, the world changes.]

xexts.scrutiny: Another history spilt… [There are Keeper-level Winter recipes that can craft this from Solomon's Preparation, or from Glassfinger Toxin]

Data:Numa.incident.base.json.label: Incident
Data:Numa.incident.base.json.desc: Base verb for Numa incident expulsion

Data:Numa.killes.json.label: Mist and Silence
Data:Numa.killes.json.startdescription: The house is quiet. The signs above the door are written in a language even I cannot read. No-one comes in answer to my knocking. Numa.

Data:Numa.rectory.json.label: Mist and Silence
Data:Numa.rectory.json.startdescription: The mists are thick, but as I approached, I saw lamplight in the Rector's study. Now, though, I see the windows are shuttered, and the light I saw was a fugitive wisp, like a lost star. Numa.

Data:Numa.smithy.json.label: Mist and Silence
Data:Numa.smithy.json.startdescription: The smithy fire still glows, but through the window I see a gaunt, eyeless shape working the bellows. There is no sign of Denzil, and I know better than to interrupt this visitor. Numa.

Data:Numatic.json.desc: This is something or someone from Numa - the time when 'seems' and 'is' cross swords with 'history' and 'eternity'.

Data:Numen.alte.json.Label: Numen: Merciless Alteration
Data:Numen.alte.json.Desc: The fundamental flaw; the irresistible shortcut; the hate that heats; the change that mars; the scar that opens. These are the foulest Histories.  [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Artist and the Archaeologist can win a particular victory.]

xexts.scrutiny: What happens when you close the book on a butterfly?

Data:Numen.asce.json.Label: Numen: the Paths of the Sun
Data:Numen.asce.json.Desc: The Sun has charted his Paths - paths beyond walls and woods and Bounds. When the Sun lights our way, when we are ready, all of us will enter Eternity - at least, in the right History... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Cartographer and the Twice-Born can win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.bala.json.Label: Numen: Back Into Balance
Data:Numen.bala.json.Desc: When the travelling Carapace-kinds passed beyond the wave and the sky, they made arrangements for their return. There are Histories where those arrangements might be invoked...  [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Executioner and the Revolutionary can win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.bell.json.Label: Numen: the Bells of Ys
Data:Numen.bell.json.Desc: Ys, by her arts, found the strike-tone that shakes the Hours. For this reason among many the Hours discourage traffic with Ys. But a bell cast with this secret could speak the Ys-note…  [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Prodigal and the Revolutionary can win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.conf.json.Label: Numen: Inescapable Confinement
Data:Numen.conf.json.Desc: Everything ultimately comes down to a choice between Eternity and History. There's only one place you're safe from both, and it's not a place anyone would want to be. It's a prison that can only exist in certain Histories...  [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Prodigal and the Archaeologist can win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.desc.json.Label: Numen: the Sun's Weakness
Data:Numen.desc.json.Desc: The Sun's sins and the Sun's scars are our salvation. There are Histories where they will trap us - prevent us rising to Eternity - [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Executioner can use it to win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.feas.json.Label: Numen: an Irresistible Feast
Data:Numen.feas.json.Desc: It was Hunger that made Worms of Dragons - when they consumed the corpses of Hours. Without the savour-secret of the Carapace, their hunger would not have been sufficient. In certain Histories, that savour-secret still has power... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Artist can use it to win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.json.label: Numen
Data:Numen.json.desc: Write a truth in a book that no-one reads. Then drop dead. No-one knows what you wrote. Unless the truth is numen. [Numina are truths so powerful that they, tentatively, believe themselves. You can use a Numen to write a new History at a suitable Desk... if you can assemble 25 of a matching Aspect.]

Data:Numen.loop.json.Label: Numen: Loopholes
Data:Numen.loop.json.Desc: When Eternity came into the world, certain prudent powers arranged loopholes: the House of the Moon, the persistence of possibility, the right to vengeance. In the right Histories, those loopholes will open again... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Twice-Born can win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.oldl.json.Label: Numen: That Old Lost Music
Data:Numen.oldl.json.Desc: In the right Histories, every song ever sung still lingers in wind and echo, untouched by the demands of Eternity…  [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Symurgist and the Magnate can win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.secr.json.Label: Numen: the Great Counterfeit
Data:Numen.secr.json.Desc: The Sun-in-Splendour and the Forge of the Days could not be joined. But Sunset Celia and the Swan King could. This secret is the trick of it. [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Twice-Born can win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.thre.json.Label: Numen: Three Rules
Data:Numen.thre.json.Desc: The Hours are bound by their own edicts - even the Chancel and the Calyptra. That's why their deepest rules are secret. In certain Histories, if we know those deepest rules, we know what even the Chancel and the Calyptra may not do.  [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Revolutionary can win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.unde.json.Label: Numen: a Final Understanding
Data:Numen.unde.json.Desc: Eternity and History cannot be reconciled. Freedom cannot be perfection - not unless we understand the paradox of the eternal ending. And only in certain Histories is that paradox possible... [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Magnate can use it to win a particular victory.]

Data:Numen.worl.json.Label: Numen: Weaving the World
Data:Numen.worl.json.Desc: The Histories, they say, are braided like hair - or tangled like roots. What is the shape of that knot? Funny you should ask…  [Any Librarian can use this to establish a History and complete the game - but the Symurgist and the Cartographer can win a particular victory.]
